# README.md

## LAST UPDATED 2026-09-23

### 📘 Overview

The Meta directory defines the entire schema ecosystem for Prismata.
It is organized into four canonical tiers, each with a clear responsibility:

Canonical — core object types and shared building blocks

Domain — domain‑specific schema families

System — runtime, tooling, and infrastructure schemas

Registry — enumerations, catalogs, and lookup tables

This structure ensures determinism, modularity, and clarity across the entire engine/editor/runtime stack.

### 📂 Folder Structure

Code
Meta/
 ├── canonical/
 ├── domain/
 ├── system/
 └── registry/
Each tier contains schema groups in subfolders ending with .schemas/.

### 1. Canonical Tier (54 Total)

Location: Meta/canonical/

Canonical schemas define core object types used throughout the system.
These are foundational and imported by nearly every other schema group.

#### 1.1 core.schemas/ (6)

Core identity and schema system:

udi.schema
slug.schema
identity.schema
metadata.schema
schema-definition.schema
schema.schema (schema‑of‑schemas)

#### 1.2 object.schemas/ (14)

Defines core object types (panes, menus, actions, etc.)

action.schema
border-pattern.schema
capability.schema
colour-role.schema
colour-scheme.schema
layout-constraints.schema
menu-binding.schema
menu-header.schema
menu-item.schema
pane.schema
pane-binding.schema
semantic-role.schema
ui-action.schema
ui-framework.schema

#### 1.3 composition.schemas/ (4)

Defines composition objects (layouts, pipelines, menu trees, etc.)

menu.schema
menu-group.schema
pane-layout.schema
ui-framework-layout.schema

#### 1.4 shared.schemas/ (18)

Reusable field blocks:

shared‑action‑fields.schema
shared-bindings.schema
shared‑border‑pattern‑fields.schema
shared-capabilities.schema
shared‑colour‑fields.schema
shared-config-fields.schema
shared-control-structures.schema
shared-geometry.schema
shared‑layout.schema
shared‑manifest‑fields.schema
shared‑menu‑fields.schema
shared‑metadata.schema
shared‑object‑header.schema
shared‑pane‑fields.schema
shared‑registry‑entry.schema
shared‑styling.schema
shared‑tag‑fields.schema
shared‑udi‑fields.schema

#### 1.5 editor.schemas/ (6)

Defines editor‑specific object types.

editor-action.schema
editor-command.schema
editor-config.schema
editor-context.schema
editor-layout.schema
editor-pane.schema

#### 1.6 engine.schemas/ (6)

Defines rendering engine object types.

glyph-renderer.schema
menu-renderer.schema
pane-renderer.schema
render-config.schema
renderer.schema
renderer-pipeline.schema

#### 2. Domain Tier (33 Total)

Location: Meta/domain/

Domain schemas define families of objects that are not part of the canonical core.

#### 2.1 capability.schemas/ (5)

Capability ecosystem:

capability.schema
capability‑group.schema
capability‑binding.schema
capability‑registry.schema
capability‑udi.schema

#### 2.2 manifest.schemas/ (7)

Manifest ecosystem:

manifest.schema
project‑manifest.schema
capability‑manifest.schema
ui‑framework‑manifest.schema
runtime‑manifest.schema
engine‑manifest.schema
editor‑manifest.schema

#### 2.3 defaults.schemas/ (5)

Default configuration:

default‑layout.schema
default‑theme.schema
default‑capabilities.schema
default‑colour‑scheme.schema
default‑border‑pattern.schema

#### 2.4 governance.schemas/ (6)

Governance and policy:

role.schema
permission.schema
policy.schema
entitlement.schema
audit.schema
governance‑manifest.schema

#### 2.5 examples.schemas/ (10)

Minimal example objects for documentation/testing.

example-action.schema
example-capability.schema
example-editor-command.schema
example-engine-renderer.schema
example-layout.schema
example-manifest.schema
example-pane.schema
example-menu.schema
example-registry-entry.schema
example-runtime-event.schema

### 3. System Tier: Location: Meta/system/ (12 Total)

System schemas define runtime, tooling, and infrastructure.

#### 3.1 runtime.schemas/ (6)

Runtime engine schemas (events, pipelines, handlers).

dispatch-table.schema
event.schema
event-loop.schema
runtime-config.schema
runtime-context.schema
runtime-state.schema

#### 3.2 tooling.schemas/ (6)

Schemas used by validators, generators, and CLI tooling.

editor-metadata.schema
introspection.schema
registry-loader.schema
schema-index.schema
schema-location.schema
schema-validator.schema

### 4. Registry Tier: Location: Meta/registry/

Registry entries are not schemas.
They define enumerations and catalogs used across the system.

menu.registry.yaml
ui‑framework.registry.yaml
colour‑scheme.registry.yaml
semantic‑role.registry.yaml
capability.registry.yaml
manifest.registry.yaml

Registry entries are consumed by:

the editor
the engine
the runtime
the schema validator
the capability system

### 📑 Schema Group Index

A complete index of all schema groups and their locations:

Other files in /Meta

### 📘 Purpose: The Meta layer provides

- a schema‑driven foundation for all Prismata objects
- deterministic validation
- consistent UDI + slug identity
- modular domain separation
- shared reusable field blocks
- a unified manifest system
- a capability ecosystem
- editor/engine/runtime integration

It is the backbone of the entire Prismata architecture.
